free_tier.stated: No user quota because there is no user write path - snapshot ingests the Debian archive itself. Scale reference from the site's own news: 'Snapshot is currently holding 172TB of data' (2024-10-08), up from 135 TB (2022) and 24 TB (2014), on 2 x 164 TB RAID6 arrays.

egress.terms: Free, two sites (Glasklar + LeaseWeb). Netfilter rate limiting was explicitly disabled ('It will be replaced by rate limiting on the HTTP layer').

tooling: apt with a dated sources.list entry, `debian-snapshot` machine-usable API at /mr/ (e.g. /mr/timestamp/), plain HTTPS. No rclone backend.
chaining: None - you cannot add content. Valuable only as a source of old Debian packages for a corpus, not as a place to put your data.
limits_note: per-object-cap: N/A (read-only). retention: total - every snapshot timestamp from 2005 to present is preserved. request-rate: HTTP-layer rate limiting in place of the old netfilter limit.
reliability_note: Read-only by construction. Included to close the category: Debian's snapshot is a preservation tool, not storage you can use. API verified live.

evidence.proved: 'Snapshot is currently holding 172TB of data'; 'The Netfilter rate limiting has been disabled ... rate limiting on the HTTP layer'
probe: GET -> 200 JSON, debian timestamps from 20050312T000000Z onward
probe: GET /archive/debian/20250101T000000Z/dists/bookworm/Release -> 302 (redirect to a dated snapshot; live)
